s: The spire that names Windhoek's skyline
w: Gottlieb Redecker's pale sandstone spire has anchored Windhoek since the German colonial years, home to the German-speaking Evangelical Lutheran Church. Every postcard of the capital finds it -- the highveld's most recognizable silhouette.
_facts: Designed by architect Gottlieb Redecker
Lutheran church belonging to the German-speaking Evangelical Lutheran Church in Namibia
historic landmark in Windhoek

w: An Anglican cathedral tucked into central Windhoek, quietly running services under its current incumbent while a church school carries on next door. No competing spires here -- just steady, unshowy congregational life.
_facts: Anglican church in Windhoek, Namibia
current incumbent is Hugh Prentice
a school is attached to the cathedral

s: The Old Fortress on Robert Mugabe Avenue
w: The Old Fortress went up as a German colonial garrison and now runs as a museum on Robert Mugabe Avenue, right next to the Independence Memorial. Windhoek's oldest building, doing time as the record of the empire that built it.
_facts: fortress and museum in downtown Windhoek
situated on Robert Mugabe Avenue
next to the Independence Memorial Museum

s: The 'Ink Palace' raised by genocide survivors' labor
w: Named for the ink its clerks burned through, the Tintenpalast was built in 1912-1913 by Herero and Nama laborers forced to work there -- survivors of the genocide the same colonial government had just carried out. It now seats Namibia's Parliament.
_facts: seat of the Parliament of Namibia
built by Sander & Kock 1912-1913 as an administration building for the German colonial government
used forced labour by Herero and Nama people who had survived the Herero and Nama genocide
named Tintenpalast for the ink used by workers

s: Twin brick towers from Windhoek's earliest years
w: Built from local materials between 1906 and 1908, St. Marien Kathedrale pairs brick Romanesque Revival arches with twin quadrangular towers crowned in white. Seat of the Archdiocese of Windhoek, and still holding daily services.
_facts: Roman Catholic church, seat of the Archdiocese of Windhoek
built 1906-1908 from local materials in brick Romanesque Revival style
flanked by two quadrangular twin towers

s: The colonial statue that got quietly boxed up
w: Unveiled in 1912 to honor German dead from the Herero and Nama genocide, the bronze rider was unmounted, re-erected, and finally taken down for good in 2013. It never left Windhoek -- just went from monument to crate, sitting in storage at the Alte Feste.
_facts: equestrian monument inaugurated 1912, honoured German soldiers and civilians who died during the Herero and Nama genocide
unmounted 2009, re-erected 2010 near Alte Feste, removed altogether in 2013
bronze statue currently in storage in the courtyard of the Alte Feste

s: The biggest of Windhoek's three hilltop castles
w: The largest of Windhoek's trio of German-built castles crowns its own hill, now doing quiet duty as the Italian ambassador's private residence. No public tours -- just a fairy-tale silhouette visible from half the city.
_facts: Schwerinsburg is the biggest of three castles in Windhoek, Namibia
today it is the private residence of the Italian ambassador in Namibia

s: The museum shaped like a coffee pot, built by North Korea
w: Locals call it the potjie, or the coffee pot, or the molar tooth -- take your pick. Mansudae, the North Korean firm, built this museum of Namibia's anti-colonial resistance on a hill flanked by a Sam Nujoma statue and a genocide memorial. History in an unmistakable shape.
_facts: history museum focused on anti-colonial resistance and national liberation
designed and built by Mansudae Overseas Projects, a North Korean firm
appearance likened to a potjie, coffee pot, or molar tooth
flanked by a statue of Sam Nujoma and the Genocide Memorial

s: A castle built for one man, named for another's wife
w: Wilhelm Sander built Heinitzburg for himself in 1914, then sold it two years later to a count who renamed it after his wife's maiden name. Now a Relais & Chateaux hotel and restaurant -- still perched over Windhoek like it owns the view.
_facts: built in 1914 by architect Wilhelm Sander for himself
sold in 1916 to Hans Bogislav Graf von Schwerin, renamed after his wife Margarete's birth name von Heynitz
used today as a restaurant and hotel, member of Relais & Chateaux

s: Windhoek's history and zoology collection, downtown
w: A government-run museum pairing Namibia's human history with its zoology under one roof in central Windhoek. No frills, just the long institutional memory of a young country, kept by the Ministry of Education, Arts and Culture.
_facts: historical and zoological museum in Windhoek
governed by the Ministry of Education, Arts and Culture of the Namibian government
